title: Chest Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: Chest pain — assess cardiac. Tachycardia common in panic.
rationale.ECG, 12 lead: Rule out MI/arrhythmia — may show sinus tachycardia only.
rationale.Cardiac troponin: Rule out MI — must be negative to differentiate from ACS.
rationale.Toxicology screen, urine: Rule out substance-induced anxiety (cocaine, amphetamines, PCP).
rationale.Reassure patient / Psychoeducation: Explain diagnosis — panic attacks are real physiological events but not dangerous. Education is therapeutic.
rationale.SSRI (Sertraline / Paroxetine / Escitalo: First-line for panic disorder. Start low, titrate slow.
rationale.Refer to psychiatry / CBT: CBT is gold standard psychotherapy for panic disorder. Psychiatry follow-up for medication management.
rationale.Benzodiazepines as sole long-term treatm: Benzos are for short-term acute management only (risk of dependence, tolerance, withdrawal). SSRIs are first-line for long-term panic disorder. CBT is essential.
rationale.Discharge without cardiac workup: Must rule out MI, PE, arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, and substance-induced anxiety. Panic attack is a diagnosis of exclusion in the ED.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea, and sense of impending doom. Symptoms peak within minutes and occur in discrete episodes. The patient has a history of similar episodes and significant anxiety about future attacks (anticipatory anxiety). This is a panic attack — a psychiatric diagnosis but one that requires thorough medical evaluation because patients often present to the ED with cardiac concerns. Key: rule out MI, PE, arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma, and substance-induced anxiety. ECG, troponin, CXR, TSH, and toxicology screen are appropriate. If negative and history consistent, panic disorder is the diagnosis. Treatment: SSRIs (first-line: sertraline, paroxetine, escitalopram) + CBT. Benzodiazepines for short-term acute management only (risk of dependence). Reassurance and psychoeducation are therapeutic.
